Latent heat of vaporization

Source: R/shared-physics.R
ef_lambda.Rd

Returns the latent heat of vaporization of water \(\lambda\), the energy needed to evaporate a unit mass of water, in J kg-1. The same function and the same method must be used everywhere in the METRIC chain (for example in the boundary condition of the cold anchor pixel and in the conversion of latent heat flux to evapotranspiration), so that the chain is internally consistent.

Usage

ef_lambda(temperature = NULL, method)

Arguments

temperature

Numeric or NULL. Air temperature [K], required by method = "fao56"; ignored (and may be omitted) by method = "constant". Must be finite and > 0.

method

Character. The formulation, with no default: the choice is a scientific decision that must be explicit. One of:

  • "constant": FAO-56 constant value, 2.45 MJ kg-1.

  • "fao56": FAO-56 function of the air temperature.

Value

Latent heat of vaporization \(\lambda\) [J kg-1]. For method = "constant", a single number. For method = "fao56", a numeric vector with the length of temperature, keeping its dim if it is a matrix or array.

Details

method = "constant" returns $$\lambda = 2.45 \times 10^{6}\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$$ the value used by FAO-56 in the simplification of the FAO Penman-Monteith equation, which corresponds to an air temperature of about 20 degrees Celsius (FAO-56, chapter 3; annex 3).

method = "fao56" evaluates FAO-56, annex 3, Eq. 3-1, $$\lambda = \left[2.501 - 2.361 \times 10^{-3} (T - 273.15)\right] \times 10^{6}$$ where \(T\) is temperature [K] (the equation is formulated with the air temperature in degrees Celsius; the conversion uses the package constant 273.15 K). FAO-56 defines \(T\) as the air temperature. At 293.15 K (20 degrees Celsius) it gives 2 453 780 J kg-1.

The surface-temperature form used in METRIC implementations is not available: its coefficient and its use of the surface temperature are CANDIDATA and must first be verified against Allen, Tasumi and Trezza (2007).

Missing values in temperature propagate to the output without errors or warnings. A missing or unknown method raises an error of class earthflux_missing_input or earthflux_unknown_method (both also earthflux_input_error). With method = "fao56", a missing or NULL temperature raises earthflux_missing_input, and non-positive or infinite temperatures raise earthflux_domain_error. A temperature range of validity of the equation is not documented by FAO-56 and is not checked.

Verification status: "constant" and "fao56" are VERIFICADA as FAO-56 values and equation.

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

See also

Other shared physical quantities: ef_air_pressure()

Examples

# FAO-56 constant value (J kg-1)
ef_lambda(method = "constant")
#> [1] 2450000

# Function of the air temperature, given in K (20 and 30 degrees C)
ef_lambda(c(293.15, 303.15), method = "fao56")
#> [1] 2453780 2430170
